# Lab 4 – Connections (Relay Control without PLC): Step-by-Step Guide

Festo training table · relays K1–K3 · bistable 5/2 valve · double-acting cylinder · pushbuttons · inductive sensor

---

## 0. Goal in One Paragraph

Build, **without a PLC**, an electro-pneumatic control: the spring-return pushbutton **SET** starts a continuous back-and-forth movement of a double-acting cylinder, **RESET** stops it. Two limit switches (S1/S2) detect the end positions, two indicator lamps show the control status. Finally test an **inductive sensor** and use it as the outer-position sensor.

---

## 1. Safety

- **Risk of crushing.** Ask the supervisor to be present before applying pressure.
- Turn off the pressure for all rewiring/repair.
- **The cylinder may start moving as soon as pressure is applied.** Keep hands out of the working area.
- 24 V DC only.

---

## 2. Components (what is what)

| Component | Function |
|---|---|
| Service unit | Filter, adjustable pressure reducer, gauge, red shut-off knob |
| Manual 3/2 valve (green button) | Spring-return; releases/blocks the air to the system |
| **5/2 valve, bistable (Y1/Y2)** | 5 ports, 2 positions; **keeps its last position**; Y1 and Y2 are two electrical pulses |
| **Double-acting cylinder** | Compressed air moves the piston in **both** directions (2 ports) |
| Limit switches S1/S2 | Electromechanical switches at the end positions |
| Relays K1, K2, K3 | K1 = latching relay (3 NO contacts), K2/K3 = 2 NO contacts each |
| Lamps H1, H2 | Show the control status |
| Inductive sensor | Detects metal; 3-wire: red = +, blue = −, black = output |

Not needed here: single-acting cylinder, 3/2 monostable valve, monostable 5/2 valve.

---

## 3. The Circuit (Figure 1) – how it works

![Circuit and pneumatic sketch](data:image/png;base64,)

| Rung | Circuit | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | +24 V → K1 contact → node → **RESET (NC)** → coil K1 → 0 V | Self-holding of K1 |
| 2 | +24 V → **SET (NO)** → node (parallel to K1 contact) | Starts K1 |
| 3 | +24 V → K1 contact → **S1** → coil K2 | While running: S1 closed → K2 |
| 4 | +24 V → K1 contact → **S2** → coil K3 | While running: S2 closed → K3 |
| 5 | +24 V → K2 contact → **Y1** | Valve pulse, drives cylinder away from S1 |
| 6 | +24 V → K3 contact → **Y2** | Valve pulse, drives cylinder back |
| 7 | +24 V → K2 contact → **H1** | Lamp 1 |
| 8 | +24 V → K3 contact → **H2** | Lamp 2 |

Sequence: SET → K1 latches. Cylinder at S1 → K2 → Y1 (+H1) → cylinder moves to S2 → K3 → Y2 (+H2) → cylinder returns to S1 → K2 → … The bistable valve remembers its position, so one pulse per direction is enough. RESET opens the K1 loop: K1, K2, K3 drop out, lamps off; the cylinder finishes the current stroke and stays in the end position.

Important details:
- **RESET must be a normally closed (NC / break) contact** – pressing it interrupts the K1 loop. In the drawing both pushbuttons look similar, so test the contact with the indicator/meter first. SET is NO.
- Do **not** change the relay numbering: K1 needs 3 NO contacts, K2 and K3 need 2 NO contacts each.
- Supply voltage can be taken from the pushbutton unit: **+ at the top, − at the bottom**.

---

## 4. Step-by-Step

### Step 1 – Study the diagrams
Read Figure 1 (electric) and Figure 2 (pneumatic). Identify each component on the table and its terminals (relay coil A1/A2, contact numbers; valve coils Y1/Y2; lamp terminals).

### Step 2 – Build the pneumatics (pressure OFF)
1. Service unit → **manual 3/2 valve** (port 1 in, 2 out).
2. Manual valve → **5/2 valve port 1** (supply).
3. 5/2 valve ports **2 and 4** → the **two ports of the double-acting cylinder**.
4. Ports 3 and 5 stay open (exhaust, internal bores).
5. Mount S1 and S2 at the two end positions of the cylinder.

### Step 3 – Build the electrical circuit (pressure and 24 V OFF)
Wire rung by rung (use short colored wires: red +24 V, blue 0 V):
1. **Rung 1:** +24 V → K1 NO contact → one side of node; RESET (NC) → K1 coil A1; A2 → 0 V.
2. **Rung 2:** SET (NO): between +24 V and the node (junction of K1 contact and RESET).
3. **Rung 3/4:** K1 NO contact (2nd/3rd contact) → S1 → K2 coil; K1 contact → S2 → K3 coil; coils to 0 V.
4. **Rung 5/6:** K2 contact → Y1; K3 contact → Y2; coils to 0 V.
5. **Rung 7/8:** K2 contact → H1; K3 contact → H2; lamps to 0 V.
6. Check every connection against Figure 1 with a finger on the diagram (rung by rung).

### Step 4 – Check, then power up
1. Have the supervisor look at the wiring.
2. Switch on the 24 V supply; test **without air**: press SET → K1 stays on; press RESET → K1 drops. Operate S1/S2 by hand → K2/K3 pull and H1/H2 light.
3. Switch on pressure (supervisor present, hands clear): press **SET** → the cylinder must run back and forth continuously; **RESET** stops it.
4. **Wrong direction / only one stroke?** Swap Y1 and Y2 wires (or S1 and S2). If the cylinder stands in the middle at start, move it manually to an end position (or briefly operate S1/S2).
5. Present the working base application to the operator/instructor.

### Step 5 – Inductive sensor
1. Connect electrically (**mechanically disconnected** so you can hold materials against it): red/brown → +24 V, blue → 0 V, black → indicator lamp → 0 V (the black wire carries 24 V when metal is detected).
2. Test with several materials (steel, aluminium, plastic, wood…): note which are detected and at what distance.
3. Mount it at the **outer position** of the cylinder piston and set a suitable distance. Find the **maximum distance** at which detection is still reliable (move the sensor away until it drops out, then back off a bit for a safety margin).
4. Optionally use it instead of S2 (black → K3 path) – only after approval.
5. Present your results; **be prepared to answer questions**.

---

## 5. Report Notes / Typical Questions

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Why a bistable valve? | Keeps its position without a permanent signal – pulses from K2/K3 are enough. |
| What does K1 do? | Latches the run state (self-holding contact), enables K2/K3 branches. |
| Why does RESET need to be NC? | It must interrupt the K1 holding circuit when pressed. |
| What happens on RESET during movement? | Valve stays in last position → cylinder finishes the stroke, stops at the end. |
| What does the inductive sensor detect? | Metal objects without contact; output = supply voltage when detected. |
| Difference single/double-acting? | Single: air one way + return spring; double: air in both directions via two ports. |

---

## 6. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause |
|---|---|
| K1 does not hold | RESET is NO instead of NC, or K1 contact not parallel to SET |
| No movement at all | Pressure off / manual 3/2 valve not open / cylinder not at S1 or S2 at start |
| Cylinder runs only one direction | Y1/Y2 coil wires mixed, or one limit switch not adjusted |
| Lamps on but valve does not switch | Valve coil on wrong terminals / 0 V missing |
| Sensor never switches | Wrong wire (black must be the output), no 0 V, too far away |
